reason: The text demonstrates multiple instances of leaders and people working together. Most clearly, Boaz (a man of prominence and property) directs his young workers to care for Ruth and facilitate her gleaning, showing cooperation between a leader and his workforce in the fields. More formally, Boaz gathers ten elders of the city at the gate and works with them alongside 'all the people' (כָּל־הָעָם) to conduct the redemption proceedings. The community witnesses and validates the transaction together: 'And all the people who were at the gate and the elders said, Witnesses you are this day.' The elders and people collectively bless the union of Boaz and Ruth, speaking favorable words together. Throughout, those in positions of influence (Boaz, the elders) collaborate with the broader community toward shared purposes.
